scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) report they cannot
reach each other, though each can still ping its own gateway (10.0.0.1
and 10.0.1.1). The odd part, per the NOC: every BGP session in the
fabric is Established and no interface has flapped -- but the spines'
routing tables no longer contain the 10.0.0.0/24 prefix at all, while
10.0.1.0/24 is still there. Investigate.

injection.action: remove the host-subnet network advertisement from BGP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 BGP network advertisement
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 (AS 65200) is supposed to advertise its host
  subnet with `network 10.0.0.0/24` under `router bgp 65200`. That
  statement was removed, so bgpd immediately withdrew the prefix; the
  spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 all lose their route to
  10.0.0.0/24 while every session stays Established. Traffic from
  pc_0_0 toward pc_0_1 is still delivered (leaf_router_0_0 still learns
  10.0.1.0/24), but the return traffic has no route back to
  10.0.0.0/24 and dies in the fabric -- so the ping fails in both
  directions.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: `network 10.0.0.0/24` missing from `router bgp 65200` on
  leaf_router_0_0
Fix: re-add the network statement on leaf_router_0_0 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Re-add the advertisement on leaf_router_0_0:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65200"
 -c "network 10.0.0.0/24"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on leaf_router_0_0 is an equally correct fix.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: BGP route origination on leaf_router_0_0. The leaf’s LAN prefix (10.0.0.0/24) is not being injected into BGP.

Mechanism: With all eBGP sessions Established, spines only install prefixes they learn. Both spines show 10.0.1.0/24 but not 10.0.0.0/24, so any traffic toward 10.0.0.0/24 has no route beyond the leaf. This explains why each host can ping its own default gateway (local L3 on the leaf) yet cannot reach the other host’s subnet.

Localization: On leaf_router_0_0, FRR is up and peering to both spines (show ip bgp summary shows 2 peers, PfxRcd 1, PfxSnt 1). However, its running config lacks any address-family or “network” statement for 10.0.0.0/24 and no redistribute policy (frr_show_running_config). The leaf is actually advertising only the remote 10.0.1.0/24 to its spines (show ip bgp neighbors … advertised-routes), confirming it is not originating its own subnet.

Root cause: The BGP configuration on leaf_router_0_0 was altered and no longer originates 10.0.0.0/24 into BGP.

Corrective fix: On leaf_router_0_0, configure origination of the LAN prefix. For example in vtysh:
router bgp 65200
 address-family ipv4 unicast
  network 10.0.0.0/24
This will cause the spines to learn 10.0.0.0/24 (and re-advertise it), restoring end-to-end connectivity. Alternatively, use “redistribute connected” with appropriate policy.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly localizes the problem to leaf_router_0_0 (mentions BGP origination missing on leaf_router_0_0 and inspects its config and peers).

per_axis.rationale: The report states the spines only have 10.0.1.0/24 and not 10.0.0.0/24, explicitly noting traffic toward 10.0.0.0/24 (the return path) has no route, explaining the ping failure.
Proposes re-adding the LAN prefix into BGP (network 10.0.0.0/24 or redistribute connected), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's logs show failed pings, BGP sessions up with only one learned prefix (RIB entries=1), and retrieved the leaf's running config and advertised-routes outputs — supporting the claim that the leaf is not originating its LAN prefix. The causal chain (missing network statement → prefix withdrawn → spines lack route → return traffic blackholed → pings fail) is logical and the key checks were performed, though many command outputs in the log are truncated and not verbatim-presented.
